title: Vessalia
imageCaption: Vessalia — bard and adventurer of Pristinia.
dek: A high elf bard finding companions, confronting the dangers of adventuring, and building a home with Di’trillio near the Lily Patch.

facts.Home: Cottage near the Lily Patch · Prima
facts.Study: Expresses a decision to accept Scribonia’s teaching offer

body:
Vessalia is a high elf bard, traveler, and adventurer making a home in Pristinia. She arrives with a lute, a ready smile, and a theatrical bow. Her first adventures bring healing, frightening encounters, difficult choices, and a growing relationship with Di’trillio. Music remains part of how she greets strangers, encourages companions, and describes what she hopes to become.

A bard at the Gate

In First Vess RP, Vessalia approaches the Gate beneath a starry sky. She introduces herself to Aurélia, who presents herself as Nébula and offers to guide her. Vessalia is unfamiliar with the place, interrupts her own daydreaming, and says she had been strolling with her lute and composing a ballad.

Nébula explains that she has arrived on Prima during a war against Death. Vessalia responds with a performative bow and offers her service. The conversation moves between flirtation, questions, and the practical need for a place to stay. She eventually heads for the tavern, thinking of a meal, a drink, and perhaps a ballad for its patrons.

Music, friendship, and the Lily Patch

The Lily Patch becomes a recurring meeting place. Vessalia returns there alone, with Aurélia, and with Di’trillio. She tries unfinished lyrics on her lute, grows frustrated when words will not come, tells jokes, dances, and looks to the stars for inspiration. These scenes show a working musician composing as she goes, rather than someone whose every song arrives complete.

Her friendship with Aurélia continues beyond that first welcome. They share conversation and affection, and later Vessalia seeks her out when she is distressed. In Selwyn’s Letter, she rests her head on Aurélia’s shoulder and eventually accepts her embrace. She explicitly reassures Aurélia that she is her friend too.

Ada’s Pristinia Press column presents a public view of the newcomer: an artist and traveler bringing music, laughter, and company into the town. That welcome is Ada’s assessment. It sits beside the smaller encounters in which Vessalia actually begins making those connections.

Learning to be useful in danger

Her first quest does not stay a lighthearted adventure. When violence breaks out between companions, she shouts for it to stop, runs to the fallen Bohlale, and kneels beside him with her hands glowing. The account describes her alarm and attempt to help without making her responsible for every outcome of the fight.

Afterward she meets Bohlale at the Pilgrim’s Hearth. She wants to be useful to the group and measures herself against people she sees as experienced fighters. In the later harpy expedition, she uses her lute and magic to help expose enemies; the record describes two harpies outlined by her spell while two escape it.

In Telomares, she is considering gathering work and earning enough to have a rapier crafted. After the dangerous quest, she tells Di’trillio that she wants to improve, support others, and help them continue when they feel unable to go on. Her wish to feel valued is spoken as a personal admission.

Di’trillio: affection and difficult conversations

Vessalia and Di’trillio’s relationship develops through shared quests, tavern conversations, walks, and time in the Lily Patch. Hand-holding, teasing, dancing, and kisses accompany conversations about trust and what each wants from the future. She becomes visibly shy when her usual fluency gives way to affection.

The relationship also includes disagreement and repair. In Clearing the Air, they discuss their fight in the Celestial Arena. Di’trillio apologizes for hurting her; she acknowledges striking first. She compares her abilities with his and worries that one wrong spell, slow response, or missed opportunity could cost someone their life. His reassurance is his view of her strengths, not proof that the fear has vanished.

In Resolution, after fleeing danger in the Before, she says she needs to work through her worry and trust that he can return without her always being there to intervene. Elsewhere she is more possessive: when Star uses the familiar name Di, Vessalia asks her to use Di’trillio instead. The affectionate relationship contains these tensions as well as its tenderness.

The Before, contamination, and Pell

Vessalia joins investigations into the Before and the harpy caves. In Back Again, she covers her mouth and nose against the haze and extinguishes her magical lights after Pell warns against magic there. The Writer explicitly describes her gaining a level of contamination as she follows Di’trillio into the haze; her own post describes nausea and unsteadiness.

A later harpy-cave post says she has always been contaminated and avoids approaching the crystals because she does not want more. These passages are preserved as different statements in the record. They do not establish the original source, duration, or full mechanics of her condition.

Pell becomes a companion in both fear and investigation. She follows him away from an unsettling presence, waits with him for the others, and looks at carvings while he offers his understanding of the world’s history. She admits that Death frightens her. His explanations remain Pell’s account, rather than becoming confirmed cosmology through her listening.

Recruitment and the need to know what she is accepting

In Dark Signs, Minerva offers Vessalia and Di’trillio a place among the Seekers, describing exploration and research into delerium while withholding details until they join. Vessalia asks what the research is for and why she is wanted. She says she has learned not to enter an arrangement without knowing what she is agreeing to.

The meeting leaves her increasingly quiet and distressed. A separate beach scene shows her shaking and crying by the sea. In the later shop conversation with Aurélia, she speaks of fearing a repeat of a life she does not want to relive. The damaged fragments do not supply a complete account of that earlier life.

In Shelter, she and Di’trillio discuss the competing offers and the possible value of the Seekers’ knowledge. She worries that Minerva may be manipulating the conversation; that remains Vessalia’s concern, not a confirmed description of Minerva’s motives. She also refuses to ask Di’trillio to abandon potentially useful research simply to relieve her own anxiety.

Severina, Camilla, and a future beyond the war

At the Tower of Gael, Vessalia introduces herself to Camilla as Vessalia the Bard, saying her titles did not come through the Gate with her. She speaks with Lady Severina about the Veilguard and with Camilla about the Hellknights, asking about protection, duties, and how those options would affect her life with Di’trillio.

Severina and Camilla explicitly leave her time to choose. The conversation records offers and consideration; it does not by itself establish a completed oath or membership in either order. Vessalia accepts armor from Severina and says she intends to fight Death for as long as she can, while hoping eventually to settle with her partner and children. Those children belong to her hoped-for future, not an established family in the scene.

A home near the Lily Patch

In Di and Vess’s Estate, Di’trillio leads her to a newly built cottage near the Lily Patch. He says he arranged its legal and material costs with Camilla, who built it. Vessalia is surprised and delighted, and says she could have helped fund it or gather supplies. He gives her a key, and they explore their home together.

Their plans include learning to cook and making a safe place to return to. Their discussions of marriage and children remain plans. In the same source, Vessalia tells him she has decided to take up Scribonia’s offer to become a student: she says she had no magic before arriving and wants to study the arcane arts seriously. In her conversation with Severina she also says a formal interview may still be pending. Completed lessons or qualifications are not established.

Welcoming the next arrival

In Vess’s First Time, the bard who once needed a guide becomes one for Star. She walks with her toward Pristinia, explains the quest board and the Pilgrim’s Hearth, and describes Fenumion as her home after years traveling the Sword Coast. Her welcome also asks a serious question about whom Star will stand beside. The scene ends with Vessalia hoping to adventure with her one day.

The surviving posts leave her continuing to learn, perform, investigate, and make a life with the people around her. They do not provide a complete chronology, settle every question about contamination, or turn every proposed allegiance into a final choice.

Vessalia in the timeline

These dates identify the surviving posts. Exact in-world dates and the complete order of the scenes remain unconfirmed. Select an event to read more.

Star’s answer on the road

The Gate record preserves Star’s reply to Vessalia’s stern appeal in greater detail. Star refuses to assume everyone from her old world is dead merely because she has been told so, while promising not to help destroy Fenumion. Vessalia apologises and asks her to help preserve both worlds; Star agrees. The exchange distinguishes a freely offered commitment from certainty about the people left behind. Read Star’s own story.

September · a gift and a dangerous return

Before the Old Earth Hills investigation, Di’trillio gives Vessalia a replacement lute decorated with a willow tree. She recognizes its connection to their shared memory and accepts it with emotion. The gesture joins an existing history of repair and affection.

The later cave fight brings her down more than once. Saoirse heals her while Moira helps Pell, and Di’trillio carries Vessalia away from the eventual collapse. Her growing willingness to help does not remove the danger or her dependence on companions. Read the cave’s outcome.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4.

The caravan · force, healing and a second chance to talk

Vessalia joins the grain caravan to Eovar, rallies its travelers and asks the party to avoid killing the attackers. Her magic still causes harm during the battle. When the slasher becomes willing to listen, Clive’s mental attack disrupts that opening; she works to restore it, offers healing and insists on speaking before more force is used.

Her later Silence around Clive is also an exercise of power over a companion. The account preserves that choice beside her negotiations rather than making her restraint absolute. Together with Velkyn’s offer, it helps secure a conditional pause in raids and a meeting with the First Hunter. Her proposed trade agreement is not yet ratified.

profile.personality: In her own posts, Vessalia greets people with jokes, music, and theatrical gestures. She also voices fear about choosing the wrong spell, asks what recruitment would require, and seeks help when overwhelmed.
profile.achievements: She intervenes when Bohlale falls, uses magic during the harpy expedition, joins investigations into the Before, and later guides Star toward Pristinia. She decides to accept Scribonia’s teaching offer; completed study is not established. Uses healing and negotiation to recover a parley and helps secure a conditional pause in caravan raids.
profile.relationships: Di’trillio is her partner, with whom she shares a cottage near the Lily Patch. Aurélia first guides her and later comforts her. Pell shares investigations, while Severina and Camilla discuss possible paths whose offers are not proof of completed membership.
